the optical anisotropy of columnar mesogens can be easily controlled by the alignment of the columns with respect to the substrate and that this control can be achieved in thin film geometry.
the optical properties of columnar liquid crystal thin films can be tuned by a proper choice of the columnar mesophase orientation and by a proper choice and concentration of the absorbing molecules.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of columnar mesogens, we can control the orientation of the columns with respect to the substrate, and we can measure their optical properties, in order to use them as active materials in photovoltaic cells.
the optical properties of discotic liquid crystal materials can be tailored by controlling the columnar orientation, and this is a promising approach to develop novel optical materials.
we have been able to determine the anisotropic refractive indices, the extinction coefficient, and the dichroic absorption ratio of columnar liquid crystals in thin films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
columnar liquid crystals are promising candidates for applications in the field of optical devices, such as waveguides, polarizers, or polarizing optical elements.
columnar mesophase thin films are promising candidates to be used in optoelectronic devices such as light emitting diodes or photovoltaic devices.
the anisotropic refractive indices of discotic columnar liquid crystals are very large and can be tuned over wide spectral ranges.
